title: English File Pre-Intermediate, File 12 (check against the book)

fixIt.text: When I got home, my sister had cook dinner.
She said me that she was tired.
He told that he was busy.
When we arrived at the station, the train had already leave.
fixIt.explain: Past perfect: had + past participle, for what happened before another past moment.

fixIt.text: I couldn't get in because I had forget my key.
fixIt.explain: had + past participle: forget, forgot, forgotten.

fixIt.text: She was hungry because she hasn't eaten all day.
fixIt.explain: The story is in the past, so the earlier action uses had: hadn't eaten.

fixIt.text: By the time the film started, we had buyed popcorn.
fixIt.explain: buy is irregular: buy, bought, bought.

fixIt.text: I didn't recognise him because he had change so much.
After she had finish her work, she went home.
When I got to class, the lesson already started.
fixIt.explain: It started before I got there: had already started.

fixIt.text: Dara said that he is tired, but he went out anyway.
fixIt.explain: Reported speech moves back a tense: "I'm tired" becomes he said he was tired.

fixIt.text: My teacher told me that I can leave early.
fixIt.explain: In reported speech, can becomes could.

fixIt.text: He asked me if I am hungry.
fixIt.explain: Reported questions move back a tense too: if I was hungry.

fixIt.text: They told us they will call back.
fixIt.explain: In reported speech, will becomes would.

fixIt.text: He said he has never seen the sea before.
fixIt.explain: Reported speech: has seen becomes had seen.

fixIt.text: Who live in that big house?
fixIt.explain: When who is the subject, there is no do: Who lives…? (he/she + -s)

fixIt.text: How many students passes the exam last term?
fixIt.explain: Last term is the past, and the subject question has no did: How many students passed?

fixIt.text: Which bus go to the airport?
fixIt.explain: Which bus is the subject, so no do, and it takes -s: Which bus goes…?

fixIt.text: What time you usually get up?
fixIt.explain: Questions in the present simple need do: What time do you usually get up?

builder.tip: When who is the subject, no auxiliary: Who wrote?
had + past participle: it happened before.

builder.text: She told me she was tired.
builder.tip: told + a person; the tense moves back.
Who is the subject: no did.

builder.text: He asked me if I was ready.
I had never seen the sea before.

radio.title: A strange evening
radio.text: Last Friday I came home late from work. When I opened the door, I saw that somebody had left the lights on. My sister told me that she had gone out at six. I asked her who had been in the house, and she said she didn't know. Then my husband called. He said that he had come home early to cook a surprise dinner, and he had gone to the shop because he had forgotten the rice.
